source: Directive tables of the Bareos 25.1.2 Director as carried by odir (crates/odir/src/commands/show_items.rs) plus Onesimus extensions (crates/odir/src/config_check.rs EXTENSIONS)
description: A Profile resource is a named set of ACLs that Console and User resources refer to, so several consoles share one definition of what they may do.

examples.title: An operator profile
examples.config:
Profile {
  Name = operator
  Description = "Run and watch backups, restore to /tmp"
  Job ACL = *all*
  Client ACL = *all*
  Storage ACL = *all*
  Schedule ACL = *all*
  Pool ACL = *all*
  File Set ACL = *all*
  Catalog ACL = *all*
  Command ACL = status, list, llist, run, rerun, cancel, restore, messages, show, .api, .help, .jobs, .clients, .storages, .pools, .filesets, .bvfs_*
  Where ACL = /tmp/bareos-restores
}

directives.name: Name
directives.description: Name of the profile; Console and User resources refer to it with Profile.

directives.name: Description
directives.description: Free text describing what the profile is for.

examples.console: configure add profile name=operator description="Run and watch backups"

directives.name: Job ACL
directives.description: Which jobs this profile may use. The list holds names or regular expressions, separated by commas or given by repeating the directive; the first matching entry decides, an entry starting with ! forbids, *all* allows everything, and a name no entry matches is forbidden. On the Onesimus Director the catalog ACL (.acl) can narrow this list further, never widen it.

examples.console: configure add profile name=operator jobacl="backup-web, restore-files"

examples.console: configure add profile name=operator clientacl="web-fd, db-fd"

directives.name: Command ACL
directives.description: Which console commands this profile may use. The list holds names or regular expressions, separated by commas or given by repeating the directive; the first matching entry decides, an entry starting with ! forbids, *all* allows everything, and a name no entry matches is forbidden. A console that may use restore needs the dot commands the restore uses as well (for the GUI: .api, .help, .bvfs_* or .ovfs_*). On the Onesimus Director the catalog ACL (.acl) can narrow this list further, never widen it.

examples.console: configure add profile name=operator commandacl="status, list, llist, restore, .api, .help"

directives.name: File Set ACL
directives.description: Which FileSets this profile may use. The list holds names or regular expressions, separated by commas or given by repeating the directive; the first matching entry decides, an entry starting with ! forbids, *all* allows everything, and a name no entry matches is forbidden. On the Onesimus Director the catalog ACL (.acl) can narrow this list further, never widen it.

directives.name: Catalog ACL
directives.description: Which catalogs this profile may use. The list holds names or regular expressions, separated by commas or given by repeating the directive; the first matching entry decides, an entry starting with ! forbids, *all* allows everything, and a name no entry matches is forbidden. A console that may use no catalog cannot list jobs or volumes. On the Onesimus Director the catalog ACL (.acl) can narrow this list further, never widen it.

directives.name: Where ACL
directives.description: Which restore target paths (the where= of a restore) this profile may use. The list holds names or regular expressions, separated by commas or given by repeating the directive; the first matching entry decides, an entry starting with ! forbids, *all* allows everything, and a name no entry matches is forbidden. An empty list forbids every where= other than the job's own; *all* allows any path. On the Onesimus Director the catalog ACL (.acl) can narrow this list further, never widen it.

directives.name: Plugin Options ACL
directives.description: Which plugin option strings a job may be started with this profile may use. The list holds names or regular expressions, separated by commas or given by repeating the directive; the first matching entry decides, an entry starting with ! forbids, *all* allows everything, and a name no entry matches is forbidden. On the Onesimus Director the catalog ACL (.acl) can narrow this list further, never widen it.
